threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when a bus driver calls you 'love' or 'darling'—trust me, it’s just part of the charm.
Last night on the 133, a couple was arguing about which chicken shop is better. It got so loud, even the driver joined in with a laugh.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a random guy in a chicken suit dancing outside the kiezkultur café while a samba band played in the background. Classic Neukölln vibes.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a bus stop where the route's been suspended because of a protest, yet folks just sit there eating döner like it's normal.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to random BART outages; the eye roll is universal, especially during Friday evening crush.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 19 Polk, taking selfies like he was in a fashion show. Classic SF—always a party on the Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab brunch anytime; locals know that the good places in Gràcia close by 4 PM, so we plan our days around it.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with the T10 tickets at the metro machine, while locals swipe effortlessly by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pause at the sound of the tube trains and look excited, while everyone else just keeps walking.
Last night on the 36, a guy sang an entire Adele song. No one clapped, but the bus driver kept smiling in the mirror.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found a street market selling fresh dill and homemade hummus right next to a graffiti-covered wall. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you stumble upon a hidden techno party in an abandoned factory at 3 AM, complete with a DIY bar and an impromptu art installation.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: If they know the difference between a 'burrito' and a 'Mission burrito,' they might be a local. Also, a true local knows to check BART delays before heading out.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy singing opera to the 38 Geary crowd while waiting for the bus. Everyone was annoyed until he hit a high note—then we clapped. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the quiet corners where local artists paint and the scent of fresh bread at 8 AM from the bakeries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their hesitation at the subway turnstiles, looking for a ticket machine that doesn’t exist in the Raval.
